title: Capacity: growth, headroom and an alert that arrives before the wall

videos.script: Every database has walls. A disk that fills. A limit on connections. A counter that runs out of numbers. {{walls}} None of them is slow. They are fine, and fine, and fine, and then the database stops. {{stop}} That is what makes capacity different from the rest of this course. A slow query complains every day. A wall says nothing until the day it arrives. {{silent}} So capacity is a forecast. How fast is each thing growing, and how far is it from its limit? Divide one by the other, and you have a date. {{date}} There is a second kind of limit, and it is not a wall at all. As a server gets busier, the time each request waits grows slowly, then suddenly. {{knee}} You will measure that curve on your own machine, and find where it bends. {{measure}} And you will write an alert that fires on the date, not on a percentage. Eighty percent full is calm if it took five years. It is an emergency if it took a week. {{alert}}
